story_report.summary: President Donald Trump named Stephen Miller as White House chief of staff, replacing Susie Wiles, with Miller set to begin Nov. 9 after the Nov. 6 announcement. The move follows midterm elections in which Democrats reportedly won control of both the House and Senate. It places a senior adviser known for hardline immigration views and for serving as deputy chief of staff for policy and homeland security adviser at the center of White House operations as the administration prepares to work with a new Congress.

sections.heading: Susie Wiles Departure Accounts
sections.body: Trump said Wiles would shift to his political operation, while Wiles said her commitment to Trump and his mission would continue in her new role. But ABC News, citing unnamed sources, reported that she submitted her resignation after Trump blamed her for the midterm losses. The chief of staff position is a White House staff appointment under the president’s authority to appoint White House Office employees, rather than a Senate-confirmed Cabinet post.

sections.heading: Miller Immigration Policy Record
sections.body: Before his appointment, Miller’s financial disclosure and the White House staff report listed him as deputy chief of staff for policy and homeland security adviser. The administration has already directed agencies to enforce immigration laws against inadmissible and removable noncitizens, expand Homeland Security Task Force coordination, pursue detention capacity and seek certain state-local enforcement agreements, subject to law and available appropriations. The White House and House Majority Whip Tom Emmer portrayed Miller as a key driver of the administration’s border policies.

sections.heading: Congressional Scrutiny of Miller
sections.body: The new Congress is scheduled by default to assemble on Jan. 3, 2027, after Democrats reportedly captured both chambers in the midterms. Rep. Robert Garcia, then the ranking Democrat on the House Oversight Committee, said Oversight Democrats would investigate Miller and challenge his policies in Congress and in court. Vice President JD Vance and Secretary of State Marco Rubio, meanwhile, called Miller a trusted and effective adviser and said they expected to work with him to advance Trump’s agenda.

unresolved.text: Public accounts differ over whether Wiles’ departure was a planned reassignment or followed her resignation after disputes over the midterm losses.
It is not yet clear whether Miller’s elevation will produce new immigration directives or operational changes, rather than tighter coordination of policies already in place.
The new Congress’s committee leadership, investigative priorities, potential requests for records or testimony, and the administration’s legal response have not been determined.

stories.title: Russian Strikes Cause Damage and Injuries in Ukraine Ahead of Upcoming Talks
stories.summary: Recent Russian strikes in Ukraine have resulted in nine injuries and significant damage to infrastructure, particularly in the Kyiv region. A kindergarten was destroyed, and firefighters responded to a major blaze as the country faces renewed attacks on its energy network. These strikes come just before trilateral talks involving Ukrainian and Russian delegations scheduled to take place in Abu Dhabi next week.

timeline_highlights.title: Trump Issues Threats Against Iranian Infrastructure Amid Strait of Hormuz Tensions

He stated that for each ship fired upon by Iranian forces, the US would respond by destroying a corresponding piece of Iranian infrastructure. This escalation comes amid ongoing tensions in the region and rising oil prices.

The threat follows continued Iranian attacks on shipping in the region.
Oil prices have surged amid the escalating tensions.

explore_lenses.summary: Ukraine’s presidency has publicly described a meeting involving Ukrainian, U.S. and Russian teams in Abu Dhabi on November 10–11. Kyiv frames it as a possible step toward leader-level diplomacy, but the public record reviewed does not confirm an agreed agenda or outcomes.

claims.text: President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said on November 3 that Ukraine expected the trilateral Ukraine-U.S.-Russia format to resume on November 10–11 at team level.
Zelenskyy said on November 4 that preparations were under way for the Abu Dhabi format and that Ukraine had provided its proposals to the U.S. side.

Ukraine’s position, as stated by Zelenskyy, is that technical talks should help pave the way for leader-level talks, which he says are needed to settle key issues for a lasting peace and security guarantees.

Zelenskyy has also argued that Europe must be included when security guarantees and Ukraine’s economic recovery are discussed; the consulted Ukrainian statements do not set out Russia’s or the U.S. delegation’s public position on the agenda.

story_report.summary: Russian strikes damaged infrastructure in Ukraine’s Kyiv region, leaving a kindergarten in ruins and prompting firefighters to battle a major blaze, according to reports and emergency-service footage. The BBC reported nine people wounded, while Euronews and Africanews put the toll at five; no reconciled total has been reported. Euronews also reported damage to energy facilities and a major bridge in Kyiv. The attacks took place before planned trilateral Ukraine-U.S.-Russia team-level talks in Abu Dhabi, for which Ukraine says preparations are under way.

sections.heading: Energy network attacks deepen civilian risks
sections.body: The latest reported damage follows a wider winter campaign against Ukraine’s energy system. The UN Human Rights Monitoring Mission documented at least 423 attacks on electricity infrastructure and 74 strikes on heating facilities between October 2025 and March 2026, saying the resulting prolonged outages affected households, hospitals, schools and other essential services. OHCHR concluded that the 2025–26 campaign appeared to violate fundamental principles of international humanitarian law.

sections.heading: Abu Dhabi talks face unresolved agenda
sections.body: President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Ukraine expected the Ukraine-U.S.-Russia format to resume on November 10–11 at team level. He said Kyiv had submitted proposals to the U.S. side and views technical discussions as a route toward leader-level talks on key issues for a lasting peace and security guarantees. Zelenskyy has also said Europe should be included in discussions of security guarantees and Ukraine’s economic recovery.

event_overview.title: About Krakow Shooting
event_overview.subject: Krakow Shooting
event_overview.summary: The Krakow shooting was a gun attack on 7 November 2026 in and around the Main Market Square in Krakow’s Old Town, Poland. Authorities reported six people killed and multiple people injured; the suspected attacker was shot and detained by police, while prosecutors opened a terrorism-related investigation.

facts.label: Date and location
facts.value: The attack occurred shortly after 3 p.m. on 7 November 2026 near Sławkowska Street by Krakow’s Main Market Square (Rynek Główny).

facts.label: Casualties
facts.value: Krakow city authorities reported six deaths and 15 injuries in the shooting.

facts.label: Suspect and police response
facts.value: The city said the alleged attacker, identified by police as a Polish citizen, was shot and detained by officers after the incident.

facts.label: Investigation
facts.value: The National Prosecutor’s Office opened an investigation covering the killing of six people in Krakow and attempted killings of others, including police officers; prosecutors described the Krakow act as a terrorism-related crime.

facts.label: Official mourning
facts.value: Poland declared national mourning for 8–9 November 2026 in tribute to the victims; Krakow separately announced city mourning through 11 November.

event_overview.scope_note: The selected timeline follows the shooting, the initial official assessment of possible far-right motives, and mourning measures, but does not attempt to cover every investigative development, victim update, or related incident.

timeline_highlights.title: Six Killed in Krakow Shooting Linked to Far-Right Ideologies
timeline_highlights.summary: A mass shooting in Krakow left six people dead, including a British national, and injured at least 17 others. The 24-year-old Polish gunman, who reportedly had far-right affiliations, was critically injured during his arrest. Authorities have launched a terrorism investigation as they explore the suspect's extremist motives. Additionally, three bodies were discovered at the gunman's home, raising further concerns about the incident.

event_overview.title: About Krakow Shooting
event_overview.subject: Krakow Shooting
event_overview.summary: The Krakow shooting was a gun attack on 7 November 2026 in and around the Main Market Square in Krakow’s Old Town, Poland. Authorities reported six people killed and multiple people injured; the suspected attacker was shot and detained by police, while prosecutors opened a terrorism-related investigation.

facts.label: Date and location
facts.value: The attack occurred shortly after 3 p.m. on 7 November 2026 near Sławkowska Street by Krakow’s Main Market Square (Rynek Główny).

facts.label: Casualties
facts.value: Krakow city authorities reported six deaths and 15 injuries in the shooting.

facts.label: Suspect and police response
facts.value: The city said the alleged attacker, identified by police as a Polish citizen, was shot and detained by officers after the incident.

facts.label: Investigation
facts.value: The National Prosecutor’s Office opened an investigation covering the killing of six people in Krakow and attempted killings of others, including police officers; prosecutors described the Krakow act as a terrorism-related crime.

facts.label: Official mourning
facts.value: Poland declared national mourning for 8–9 November 2026 in tribute to the victims; Krakow separately announced city mourning through 11 November.

event_overview.scope_note: The selected timeline follows the shooting, the initial official assessment of possible far-right motives, and mourning measures, but does not attempt to cover every investigative development, victim update, or related incident.
